title: Refinement cochain map along a scheme morphism
statement: Let f:X'\to X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], U=(U_i)_{i\in I} and U'=(U'_a)_{a\in I'} families of opens, c:I'\to I with U'_a\subset f^{-1}(U_{c(a)}), and F an O_X-module. Use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the ordered Cech complexes [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]. The refinement cochain map gamma:Cech(U,F)\to Cech(U',f^*F), after forgetting global-section scalars, is characterized in degree n by gamma(s)_{a_0\ldots a_n}=(f^*s_{c(a_0)\ldots c(a_n)})|_{U'_{a_0\ldots a_n}}, where pullback of sections is the unit of tensor pullback adjoint to pushforward. The component rule defines a unique additive cochain map for every such family and refinement; no cover or finiteness hypothesis is needed for this construction. Its cohomology map uses the canonical comparisons between homology and forgetting scalars.

source.place: Tag 01FD, cohomology-lemma-functoriality-cech: the tuple formula defining gamma

proof.text: Use the unit of the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For each degree and refined tuple, compose evaluation at its refined original tuple, the additive unit component on that original intersection, and restriction to the refined intersection. AddMonoidHom.pi bundles these components into an additive map between the explicit groups of Cech cochains.

Expand both differentials with TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplex_d_apply. Additivity moves the unit and restriction through the finite sums and integer multiples. For each omitted vertex, PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply moves the original restriction past the unit. Functor.map_comp composes the remaining restrictions. The two composites have the same endpoints in the category of opens, so they are equal by subsingleton elimination. This proves the degree maps commute with the differential and defines a map of the explicit complexes.

Conjugate the explicit cochain map by the proved TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplexFunctorIso isomorphisms on the source and target. Their degree components are cechComplexFunctorXAddEquiv. The identity AddEquiv.apply_symm_apply proves the required component formula. Any other map with that formula agrees after each degree equivalence and every tuple evaluation; injectivity of the equivalence and extensionality of complex morphisms prove uniqueness. No cover, finiteness, injectivity or acyclicity condition enters this argument.
